authorization: Researcher asked the program to step back, use the reference literature, and identify scientifically important questions beyond incremental phase-diagram polishing.
question: Can the decoder-independent distribution of DeltaF=log(Z0/Z1) be turned into a physically interpretable order-parameter and scaling protocol that distinguishes correctable, finite-risk and BKT-like regimes?
claim_boundary: This synthesis may define observables and a discriminating protocol from existing evidence and literature; it cannot infer scaling or universality without new registered size data.
alternatives: Typical stiffness: |DeltaF| grows in probability and Bayes risk vanishes.
Finite-gap phase: DeltaF retains positive O(1) mass and intrinsic Bayes risk remains nonzero.
Broad rare-event mixture: typical gaps grow but rare near-zero gaps dominate risk, requiring tail rather than mean scaling.
planned_steps: Synthesize exact posterior-gap identities, existing finite distributions and the Temkin/Hauser statistical-mechanics mappings without adding samples.
Define reader-facing scaling observables that separate median stiffness, near-zero gap mass and Bayes-risk tails.
Preregister the smallest future size/noise matrix only if existing data cannot discriminate the alternatives.
acceptance_criteria: The observable is defined directly from physical sector partition sums and does not depend on a path selector or practical decoder.
The protocol distinguishes typical, near-zero-tail and risk-weighted behavior and states what each implies physically.
Existing data are used only within matched geometry, channel and observation contracts; no Lab 003 pooling or threshold fit is allowed.
Any new acquisition is separately preregistered with boundary-focused sampling and uncertainty before it begins.
stop_rule: Do not collect new samples, fit a threshold, claim BKT universality or reuse practical-decoder LER as intrinsic risk. Stop after the order-parameter synthesis and a go/no-go acquisition decision.
decision: The exact identity R_L=E[(1+exp(abs(DeltaF)))^-1] makes the full posterior-gap distribution a decoder-independent order parameter. Existing L=5,7,9 p=.30 records do not distinguish typical stiffness, persistent finite gaps and rare-tail-controlled risk. Register the smallest boundary-focused q=.90,.94,.97 and L=7,9,11 matrix; do not sample in this synthesis tick.
